title: Hotpatch safety & signal scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for reviewing and landing tiny hotpatch PRs with minimal blast radius. Focus: emergent latency spikes and a small KV cache bug that causes stale prefix reuse under rare race condition. Not a spec — dump of heuristics, checkpoints, and follow-ups to keep the change safe.

High-level constraints (remind self):
- patch must be <= 6 files changed, mostly in runtime/cache layer
- no blocking DB migrations, no schema changes
- behavioral change should have a clear, small-surface canary path (1% traffic or internal-only route)
- must include rollback trigger and post-rollout signal checks

Quick checklist for each hotpatch PR:
- owner + primary reviewer assigned (explicit)
- clear one-line summary + risk note in PR description
- small test harness included (unit + a synthetic integration test that simulates concurrent requests)
- changelog entry (internal) and JIRA link in PR body
- rollout plan: canary gate, metrics to watch, rollback criteria

Suggested canary gating signals (minimal set):
1) latency p50/p95 on the target route (compare to baseline window: last 30m pre-deploy).
2) token throughput per instance — sudden drop could mean blocking path.
3) error rate (5xx) and specific new error signatures.
4) KV cache hit ratio and 'prefix reuse' count if we have the metric.
5) tail latency histogram (if histogram available) — watch >99.9th.
If any of these deviate by more than threshold -> auto-fallback. Thresholds: p95 +20% OR error rate +0.1% absolute OR cache-hit drop >3%.

Quick review notes for concurrency-sensitive fixes:
- look for unsynchronized writes to shared maps (double-check comments where we touch cache.put and cache.get).
- ensure code uses existing sharding/lock helpers (don't invent ad-hoc locks).
- prefer compare-and-swap or atomic ops where possible; if adding synchronized block, keep it minimal and document latency trade-off.
- thread-safety tests: spin up 8 concurrent goroutines/threads, run 10k operations mixing get/put, assert invariants (no stale prefix returned more than X times).

Manual test recipe (local or CI container):
1) build runtime image: make build-runtime-local
2) run with small synthetic load: ./run_local --routes=replicaA --concurrency=16 --scenario=prefix-stress
3) tail logs for lines tagged [kv-cache] and grep for 'stale-prefix' occurrences
4) run provided integration test: go test ./runtime -run TestHotpatchPrefixRace --bench=false

PR review heuristics (what I personally look for):
- PR description: concise rationale + fallback plan present. If missing -> request update.
- Test coverage: if no concurrency unit test -> request one.
- Metrics: does this change affect existing dashboards? any added instrumentation? If none, ask to add.
- Complexity: prefer simpler approach even if slightly suboptimal. Performance micro-optimizations can be follow-ups.
- Observability: Is there a feature flag or debug metric to enable verbose tracing? Add an opt-in to avoid noisy logs.

Immediate follow-ups post-merge (my checklist):
- Kick off 1% canary for 30 minutes, then 10% for 1 hour, then 100% if stable (see rollout playbook).
- Check the five signals above at 5m, 15m, 30m, 60m buckets. Take screenshots and paste into JIRA comment.
- If anomaly, flip traffic to previous variant and open incident link. Document rollback reason in the PR.

Longer-term ideas (notes to self / maybe product):
- add a small "prefix-reuse" metric emitted from runtime whenever cache returns a value that was older than X ms — helps quantify impact.
- tiny chaos test in nightly that injects reordered cache events to simulate the race.
- consider enabling a runtime-level ASAN-like mode for debug builds to surface concurrency misuse in dev.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- What is acceptable stale-prefix rate in production? (ask SRE/observability team) -> add to doc when answered.
- Does dedicated capacity customers see different cache behavior due to pinning? (ask infra)
- Should we automatically instrument prefix age on every cache hit or sample-based? add cost estimate.

Notes to reviewers (copy into PR template if useful):
- This change targets an edge race in the prefix KV cache. It reduces probability of returning stale prefix by introducing CAS on the cache entry update. The trade-off is an additional atomic CAS on hot-path; I measured ~1.6% median latency overhead in microbenchmarks. Canary will validate real-world impact.

Random: slack threads: #runtime-ops pinned messages about previous cache incident (2025-11) are relevant. Confluence: "kv-cache-design" page has background.

End of scratchpad. Keep this lightweight — move to a proper PR checklist template if we repeat this flow more than twice.
